paragraphs.title: Moses’ Introduction and the General Laws of Vows

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses spake unto the heads of the tribes concerning the children of Israel.”
easy.q: To whom did Moses speak concerning the children of Israel?

answers: The matter Moses was about to explain
easy.explanation: Moses said, “This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded.”

answers: Do according to all that proceeds from his mouth
easy.explanation: The passage says, “He shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.”
easy.q: What must a man do after making a vow or oath?

answers: He delivers the Lord’s command through this instruction
He asks them to cancel every vow
He says that oaths need not be kept
medium.explanation: Moses addresses the heads of the tribes and gives them the command of the Lord.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Moses speaking to the tribal leaders and the laws that follow?

answers: He must not repeat his words
He must not violate his vow
He must not write his words
medium.explanation: The phrase teaches that a person must not break or disregard a vow.
medium.q: What does “he shall not break his word” mean?

answers: To emphasize responsibility for spoken commitments
To limit vows to tribal leaders
medium.explanation: The wording emphasizes that a person is responsible for fulfilling his spoken promise.
medium.q: Why does the passage say that a man must do what proceeds from his mouth?

answers: Israel speaks to Egypt, and Egypt answers Moses
Moses receives the Lord’s command and speaks to the tribal leaders
The tribal leaders cancel Moses’ words
challenge.explanation: The verses show Moses speaking to the tribal leaders about the command of the Lord.
challenge.q: Which sequence is presented in these verses?

challenge.explanation: Both a vow and an oath are presented as spoken commitments that must be honored.
challenge.q: What does the pairing of a vow and an oath suggest?

answers: Human words have no lasting meaning
challenge.explanation: The command to fulfill vows and oaths shows that binding speech has practical importance.
challenge.q: What is the central principle in this opening section?

paragraphs.title: The Vows of a Young Woman in Her Father’s House

easy.explanation: The verse describes her as being “in her father’s house in her youth.”
easy.q: Where is the young woman when she makes her vow?

answers: The vow is transferred to the tribal leaders
easy.explanation: If her father remains silent, “all her vows shall stand.”
easy.q: What happens if her father hears her vow and holds his peace?

answers: On the day he hears it
easy.explanation: The passage says he must disallow her “in the day that he heareth.”
easy.q: When must the father disallow the vow in order to cancel it?

answers: The vow is transferred to her husband
medium.explanation: The text says that when her father holds his peace, her vows and bonds stand.
medium.q: What is the result of the father’s silence on the day he hears the vow?

medium.explanation: The father can reject the vow, preventing it from standing.
medium.q: What does “disallow” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The verse says that none of her vows or bonds “shall stand.”
medium.q: What happens if the father disallows the vow on the day he hears it?

answers: The father’s response on the day he hears it
The number of vows she made
The location of the tribal leaders
challenge.explanation: Both the father’s silence and his objection are considered on the day he hears the vow.
challenge.q: What condition is involved both when the vow stands and when it is canceled?

answers: It functions as permission for the vow to stand
It requires the young woman to vow again
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the father’s silence with the vows standing.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the father’s silence?

answers: Because her father canceled the commitment
Because she never heard her father
challenge.explanation: The verse says the Lord shall forgive her because her father disallowed her.
challenge.q: Why does the Lord forgive her when her father disallows the vow?

easy.explanation: The verses describe the husband hearing the woman’s vow.
easy.q: Who hears the woman’s vow when she has a husband?

easy.explanation: If he remains silent, her vows and bonds stand.
easy.q: What happens when the husband hears the vow and holds his peace?

easy.explanation: The passage says that every vow of a widow or divorced woman “shall stand against her.”
easy.q: What is said about the vow of a widow or a divorced woman?

answers: Agreement for the vow to stand
A rejection of the woman’s words
medium.explanation: When the husband holds his peace, the vows and bonds stand.
medium.q: What does the husband’s silence on the day he hears the vow signify?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the words and vows that came from her mouth.
medium.q: What does “proceeded out of her lips” refer to?

answers: He makes the vow of none effect
The vow is transferred to her father
medium.explanation: The husband can make the vow “of none effect” when he disallows it that day.
medium.q: What happens if the husband disallows the vow on the day he hears it?

answers: The widow’s or divorced woman’s vow stands, while the husband may establish or cancel a married woman’s vow in the stated cases
A widow’s or divorced woman’s vow is never recognized
A married woman cannot speak a vow
challenge.explanation: The passage says the widow’s or divorced woman’s vow stands, while it describes the husband’s authority regarding a wife’s vow.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the vows of a widow or divorced woman and those of a married woman?

answers: The response on that day determines whether the vow stands
The time of hearing does not matter
Only a response many years later matters
challenge.explanation: The passage repeatedly connects the result of the vow with the husband’s response on the day he hears it.
challenge.q: What does the repeated reference to the day of hearing show?

answers: The vow returns to her father
challenge.explanation: The text says, “Then he shall bear her iniquity” if he makes the vow void afterward.
challenge.q: What is the result of canceling the vow after the husband has already remained silent?

paragraphs.title: Summary of the Laws of Vows

answers: A man and his wife, and a father and his daughter
easy.explanation: The verse names the relationship between a man and his wife and between a father and his daughter.
easy.q: Between which relationships are these statutes summarized?

answers: Her youth in her father’s house
easy.explanation: The verse says, “being yet in her youth in her father’s house.”
easy.q: What stage of the daughter’s life is mentioned?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “These are the statutes, which the Lord commanded Moses.”
easy.q: Who commanded these statutes to Moses?

answers: To summarize the relationships covered by the statutes
To add a new law about warfare
medium.explanation: The verse summarizes the laws in relation to a man and his wife and a father and his daughter.
medium.q: What is the purpose of this final verse?

medium.explanation: The word refers to the laws or regulations commanded by the Lord.
medium.q: What does “statutes” mean in this context?

answers: It summarizes the laws about fathers, daughters, husbands, and wives
It changes to an unrelated journey
It describes a battle in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The final verse gathers together the family relationships discussed in the preceding laws.
medium.q: How does this verse relate to the earlier verses?

answers: The chapter addresses vows within particular family relationships
The chapter concerns only national leaders
The laws have nothing to do with vows
challenge.explanation: The summary places these vow laws within two specific family relationships.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the description of the laws as applying between a man and his wife and a father and his daughter?

answers: They were commanded by the Lord to Moses
They were created only by the fathers
They were established by the husbands
challenge.explanation: The verse directly identifies the Lord as the one who commanded Moses.
challenge.q: What does the ending emphasize about the source of these statutes?

answers: She is still young and in her father’s house
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that the daughter is still in her youth in her father’s house.
challenge.q: Which detail limits the description of the relationship between the father and daughter?
